assessment.summary: BTK (Q06187) is an exceptionally well-validated drug target with 170 PDB structures (best resolution 1.08Å), 21,674 ChEMBL IC50 entries (median 12 nM), and 6 approved drugs including ibrutinib, acalabrutinib, zanubrutinib, and pirtobrutinib. The target has strong disease validation in B-cell malignancies and primary immunodeficiencies, with active ongoing research into next-generation inhibitors and PROTACs. Druggability is unambiguously high across all evidence dimensions.
evidence_gaps: Resistance mechanisms to covalent BTK inhibitors (e.g., C481S mutation) are well-documented but optimal strategies to overcome them remain an active research area
Long-term safety profiles of newer non-covalent inhibitors (e.g., pirtobrutinib) are still being established in real-world settings
PROTAC-based BTK degraders are in early-stage discovery; clinical validation is pending
Selectivity profiles across the full kinome for all approved agents are not uniformly characterised, leaving off-target liability questions partially open
Biomarker-driven patient stratification for BTK inhibitor response remains incompletely defined
